transcript:
User: Yeah, what.
Agent: Hey, you’re through to Linda with Dialux — I handle the intro and scheduling for our team.  

What made you call in today?
User: Didn't call you. You called me. What's this about?
Agent: Got it, thanks for calling back.  

Yeah, you’re speaking with Linda on Jay’s team at Dialux — we work with businesses that lose customers when calls go unanswered. Were we trying to reach you about your business line or is this your personal cell?
User: Business line. Szymanski & Sons Plumbing. Unbelievable.
Agent: Ah, got it — Szymanski & Sons Plumbing, and you’re saying “unbelievable” about the business line.  

When a call comes in and you’re out on a job or under a sink, who’s actually picking up that line right now?
User: No one picks up. Missed calls. Sure, sure.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — no one picks up, missed calls, it adds up.  

So on a typical day for Szymanski & Sons, how many calls would you guess are going to voicemail or just not getting answered at all?
User: About 9 missed calls a week. Unbelievable.
Agent: Wow, yeah — about 9 missed calls a week for plumbing work is a lot, that’s real money walking away.  

When those folks don’t get you on the first try, do you feel like they usually call back later, or are they probably just dialing the next plumber on Google?
User: Maybe half call back. Rest find someone else. Spare me.
Agent: Yeah, I get it — if only half call back, that’s like 4–5 plumbing jobs a week just handed to the next guy, which is brutal.  

If there were a way where every one of those calls got picked up right away, booked, or at least texted back automatically while you’re on a job, is that something you’d even want to hear about, or not worth your time?
User: Sure, sure. Might be worth it. But get to the point.
Agent: Got it, I’ll keep this tight.  

So with about 9 missed calls a week right now, has anyone ever actually walked you through what that’s costing Szymanski & Sons in lost jobs, or no?
User: No walkthrough. Just know it's lost money. Unbelievable.
Agent: Yeah, totally get it — you just feel the money slipping, even if no one’s shown you the numbers.  

Mind if we do a super quick back-of-the-napkin on it using your 9 missed calls a week, just so you can see what you’re actually leaving on the table?
User: Fine, but make it quick. Average job's $380. Unbelievable.
Agent: Got it, $380 a job — that’s helpful.  

And out of those 9 missed calls a week, what percentage do you think would’ve turned into paying jobs if someone had picked up — maybe half, 60%, something else?
User: Yeah, maybe half would've booked. But enough of this.
Agent: Totally, I’ll cut to it — using your numbers, that’s about $1,710 a week walking out the door, around $7,400 a month in missed plumbing jobs.  

If we could stop that bleed by making sure every call gets picked up and booked even when you’re on a job, would you actually move on something like that, or are you just curious right now?
User: Sure, sure, but what's your plan? Unbelievable, get to it.
Agent: Totally fair, I hear you — you’re leaking about $7,400 a month, so let me get straight to it.  

So… it’s a 20‑minute walkthrough where we show you exactly how we stop those missed calls from slipping to competitors and what that looks like on your numbers — what’s better for you, later today or sometime tomorrow?
User: Fine, fine. Tomorrow works. Keep it short.
Agent: Got it, tomorrow and keep it tight.  

Quick thing before I lock in a time with Jay — what’s your first name, so I know who he’s meeting with?
User: Gene. You got it now? Unbelievable. Just book it already.
Agent: Got you, Gene — thanks for sticking with me.  

Earliest I can get you is Thursday in Central time: we can do 10:45 or 11:30 in the morning — which one’s less unbelievable for you?
User: Central time, fine. 10:45. Just book it. Unbelievable how long this took.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that for you, Gene.
Agent: Alright Gene, you’re all set — you and Jay are booked for Thursday at 10:45 in Central time, and you’ll get a text with the details so you can change it if you need to. Really glad we got this locked in for Szymanski & Sons Plumbing; before I let you go, is there anything else you need from me right now?
